chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about what necessitates expiation from oaths. He said: 'Whatever was obligatory upon you to do, and you swore not to do it, then you did it, there is nothing upon you when you do it; and whatever was not obligatory upon you to do, and you swore not to do it, then you did it, upon you is the expiation.'
ai.seo_question: When is expiation required for breaking an oath not to do something?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between oaths regarding obligatory duties versus voluntary acts, establishing that breaking an oath not to perform a wajib incurs no expiation, whereas breaking an oath not to perform a mustahabb act does. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the nature of the act sworn against, ensuring that the legal burden of kaffarah aligns with the specific category of the deed, thereby preventing unnecessary financial or ritual penalties for fulfilling divine commands.
